original_test_intent: Verify that every applicable E1.S backplane has the correct board-level FRU identity and service fields, mapped to its chassis location and slot group, and that BMC Web shows the same backplane information.
original_method: The storage/platform owner maps backplane assemblies and slot ranges to stable FRU devices, provides board-level expected fields, then an agent captures the complete inventory and compares only the mapped backplane records while preserving attached-drive and link health; an operator confirms Web parity.
manual_activity: The owner enumerates E1.S backplane assemblies, physical slot ranges and FRU/Web identities, supplies board-level truth and reviews mismatches. No drive removal, rescan or I/O is required for this FRU row.
required_inputs: Chassis and E1.S backplane count/location/side/slot-range map
Backplane PN/revision/serial and BMC/FRU firmware identity
Per-backplane FRU device/area and BMC-Web object
Rules separating backplane identity from individual E1.S drive FRUs
Attached E1.S device/slot/link/namespace baseline only for non-disturbance verification
Secret-safe read access, log retention and storage recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not accept every FRU containing E1.S as the backplane record
Bind each record to physical backplane and slot range before comparison
Retain complete inventory and record boundaries; do not use six trailing lines as full evidence
Do not remove drives, rescan PCIe, reset links/controllers, write storage or change namespaces
Do not edit FRU, update firmware or clear SEL/OS logs
Protect credentials and redact only secrets
Stop on drive/namespace/link disappearance, duplicate backplane identity, malformed FRU, BMC or storage anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Verify source identity and applicable backplane/slot topology
Collect complete FRU inventory via approved BMC access
Resolve board-level FRU records and compare their full required fields
Prepare exact Web objects for operator parity review
Verify storage and management state remained stable
Perform no I/O workload, physical handling, write, rescan or verdict action
engineer_actions: Define board versus drive identity fields and expected values
Confirm Web representation and optional-field policy
Evaluate mapping/identity/storage anomalies and decide result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The complete `fru print` source is relevant, but `grep -iA6 E1.S Backplane` may truncate the record, miss differently named assemblies or match a drive/other E1.S object. It does not prove slot association, expected fields or Web parity and exposes the password in argv.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive the complete FRU inventory through approved secret-safe access, select each backplane by stable FRU ID plus physical slot-range mapping, compare the full board-level field oracle and then correlate the exact BMC-Web object.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: E1.S BP, FRU list, readable/correct/Web criteria and 10/10-minute estimates remain; no backplane count, slot range, FRU ID or storage action is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES E1.S BACKPLANE TOPOLOGY AND FRU FIELD PACKAGE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map chassis backplanes to slot groups and FRU devices, retain complete records, compare board identity separately from drive inventory, validate each Web object and prove NVMe enumeration/links were unchanged by the read-only query.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical slot-range provenance and a strict backplane-versus-drive boundary without changing the passive FRU intent.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A readable E1.S-labelled snippet cannot prove which backplane or all installed assemblies; NVMe drive enumeration proves data-path presence, not backplane FRU correctness.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Although FRU reads are passive, an incorrect backplane-to-slot map can misdirect field replacement or storage service and make failures appear on the wrong drive group.

project_override_considerations: Integrated or non-FRU backplanes require an explicit parent-FRU ownership/applicability decision. A project may use vendor-specific Web/API labels, but must preserve stable physical slot-range correlation and must not substitute drive FRUs.
expected_evidence: Source variant, chassis and BMC/FRU/backplane firmware identity
Physical backplane locations and exact E1.S slot-range/population map
Per-backplane stable FRU device/area and Web object
Approved board-level field, optional-value and normalization matrix
Complete redacted raw FRU inventory with status
Decoded per-backplane comparison distinct from drive FRUs
Web parity plus before/after NVMe device/namespace/link/error and BMC/SEL/OS health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently names an E1.S backplane FRU and Web comparison. It omits topology and field values but does not conflate backplane and drive identities in the Master text.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive backplane FRU comparison is well defined once the project supplies topology and expected fields. Those inputs are obtainable and do not require guessing or active storage operations.

review_improvement: Requires physical slot-range provenance and separates backplane records from drive FRUs, preventing a generic E1.S text match or healthy NVMe enumeration from producing a false identity result.
independent_technical_reasoning: E1.S systems can have multiple backplanes and many drive FRUs whose names share the same token. The acceptance object is the backplane assembly, so evidence must tie a complete FRU record to a physical slot group before comparing fields. Storage inventory is useful only to prove non-disturbance, not correctness. This makes a bounded read-only workflow possible after mapping, with no need for physical drive actions.
